subject: EdgeKit / Redwood connector: support bridge + escalation protocol
messages:
From: EdgeKit Support <support@edgekit.io>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@edgekit.io>, sre@nimblehealth.com
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 18:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: connector timeouts impacting NimbleHealth (urgent)

Hi Rishi,

We started seeing repeated connector timeouts to Redwood’s embeddings endpoint when processing NimbleHealth daily batch jobs. Errors started ~2026-11-14 02:00 UTC and we've observed retries that push downstream latency beyond the customer SLA. NimbleHealth is escalating.

Sample symptoms:
- 504 gateway errors during continuous batch window (see attached logs).
- Sporadic tokenization failures on long payloads (~> 12k chars).
- Automatic retry floods from our side causing request spikes.

We need the following from Redwood ASAP:
1) A primary on-call contact and escalation ladder for partner-impact incidents.
2) A temporary config we can apply to back off retries or route to a fallback model during the incident.
3) Contact to join an emergency bridge (we can be available now).

Attachments: 1 (nimblehealth-error-log-20261114.txt)

Thanks,
EdgeKit Support
support@edgekit.io
EdgeKit | Platform Integrations
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: EdgeKit Support <support@edgekit.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 07:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: connector timeouts impacting NimbleHealth (urgent)

Thanks for flagging this — sorry for the disruption to NimbleHealth. I’m escalating and looping in our partner engineering and CS teams.

Immediate plan:
- Ben (partner eng) will triage root cause on the connector and propose a temporary routing/rate-limit change.
- Marissa/Tessa will coordinate communication with NimbleHealth and own the external bridge while we triage.
- I’ll propose a formal 72-hr support bridge and an escalation ladder that we can sign off on to avoid future ambiguity.

Request for EdgeKit: please confirm you can join a live bridge at 09:00 PST (two-hour window) so we can capture logs and run test payloads. If earlier, tell us; we’ll try to make space.

I’ve attached a working draft of an escalation ladder for quick review — this will be a short-term addendum to the partner SLA and does not change the core contract.

Attachments: 1 (redwood-edgekit-escalation-ladder.docx)

—
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, EdgeKit Support <support@edgekit.io>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: connector timeouts impacting NimbleHealth (urgent)

On it — quick notes from triage:
- Errors appear correlated to ~12k+ payload sizes and a specific sequence-length path that triggers fallback kernel paths. That path can time out under retry storms.
- Short-term mitigation: apply a soft client-side rate limit and enable a lighter-weight model variant for long payloads to reduce per-token latency.
- I can push a rate-limit config to EdgeKit’s connector (non-breaking) that will cap burst concurrency to 8 requests and add an exponential backoff header. We should monitor for 3 business cycles.

Ask EdgeKit: we’ll need a short-lived SSH-enabled debug session or temporary S3 access to collect detailed traces (I’ll provide an upload token and instructions). If EdgeKit prefers not to share that level of access, we can run a paired live test session on the bridge and capture enough info.

I’m happy to join the 09:00 PST bridge.

Attachments: 1 (rate-limit-patch.diff)

—
Ben Carter
Principal Partner Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Olivia Tran <olivia.tran@edgekit.io>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: EdgeKit Support <support@edgekit.io>, sre@nimblehealth.com, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: connector timeouts impacting NimbleHealth (urgent)

Thanks — we can join the 09:00 PST bridge. We’ve invited NimbleHealth SRE on their side and scheduled a 60-minute emergency session.

On access/sharing: EdgeKit can provide temporary S3 logs and we’ll open an upload for the traces Ben needs. We prefer paired debugging rather than SSH access.

On SLA: NimbleHealth is asking for a short-term operational retainer (24/7 bridge coverage + priority triage) while we stabilize. We reviewed Redwood’s draft escalation ladder and propose a minor contractual addendum. I’ve started a DocuSign envelope for a 90-day operational retainer amendment so we can get the bridge standing quickly: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/SigningLink?envelopeId=abc-123-edgekit

Please confirm you have an authorized signatory to execute the amendment and confirm billing contact — we’ll expedite once signed.

—
Olivia Tran
Director, Platform Partnerships | EdgeKit
